data.name: Andromeda
data.short_meaning: In Greek mythology, Andromeda was a princess chained to a rock as a sacrifice to a sea monster. Saved by Perseus.
data.long_meaning: Andromeda is a mythological princess in Greek mythology, who was chained to a rock as a sacrifice to a sea monster. She was saved by Perseus, who freed her and married her. The name is derived from the Greek words 'ander' (man) and 'mede' (in the middle), suggesting a 'man in the middle' or 'chained one'. This name carries the symbolic message of sacrifice and redemption.
data.spiritual_meaning: Andromeda represents the strength and beauty of the universe and the power of love to overcome adversity.

data.cultural_impact: To Christians, Andromeda represents the sacrifice and redemption of Jesus Christ. In the biblical story of Andromeda, she is saved by Perseus – a symbol of Jesus, who saves humanity from sin and suffering. The name carries a powerful reminder of the human condition, and our need for salvation.
data.spiritual_significance: Andromeda also symbolizes the spiritual journey of every individual. Chained to the rock of our own pride, prejudice, and shortcomings, we often feel helpless and unable to break free. But just as Perseus freed Andromeda, so too does Christ free us from the bondage of our own limitations. The name Andromeda serves as a reminder of our inherent worth and dignity, and the power of redemption and forgiveness to transform even the most difficult circumstances.
